utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. We are Tuesday, the 12th of January, 2010. I would like to welcome our witness. Colonel, I hope that you had a good evening. I also like to wish a good day to all the accused present and members of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday we finished off quickly because we had gone beyond 7.00 p.m., and I had a few follow-up questions for you which I'm about to put to you very briefly. I'm not going to delve into the details, but we have already heard a number of witnesses, and we have a number of documents that stated that shelling had taken place on the 11th of September, 1993, where the Muslim neighbourhood of Mostar was shelled. Purportedly, there were three dead and 20 people injured. On transcript page 10.158, 13th of September, 1993, grenades purportedly and anti-tank shots which have caused three dead and 2 people wounded. Witness CB, page number 10.159. Mr. Cedric Thornberry came in August, who was working for UNPROFOR. He stated that East Mostar had not been spared by the shelling. Transcript page 26.166. In the month of September -- I shall run from September to October. In September we have a report, Exhibit Number 05428, mentioning five shell impacts coming from the area controlled by the HVO; five dead, 13 wounded. I spent part of the night looking into this, Exhibit 5625, because I wanted to put questions to you. This is Mr. Larry Forbes who explains that the East Mostar hospital was targeted by artillery fire from the 4th to the 5th of October, 1993. We have several witnesses and several documents that mention artillery fire. So this is my question: In respect of the recent case law on the Drago Milosevic case, the Judges need to establish whether or not there were any casualties, and the Judges need to establish where the shots came from, because if we cannot establish that, it is impossible for us to charge the accused, and this is the case law of the Appeals Chamber in this case. So I would like to address these three possibilities: (A) the HVO fires intentionally. Perhaps there were any written orders which I have not seen so far; or, (B) the HVO responds and fires back either from a fire coming from the Serb area or fires back against the ABiH, and if there is firing back, then there is collateral damage. That's one of the ideas. Second, the Serbs fire, and we have documents that indicate that the Serbs were using artillery fire, I won't go into the details of this because we do have documents to that effect, and then civilians are hit by the Serb fire; or the second sub-possibility, the Serbs fire, the HVO fires back, and then there -- there are casualties among the civilians because fires -- the shots were fired quickly and not well calculated, and the shells did not fall on the Serb side but fell within the lines controlled by the ABiH, and you explained to us in detail yesterday that between you and the Serbs there was East Mostar. That is the second possibility. But we also have a third possibility which is the following: i.e., the Muslims themselves for political or other reasons might have fired at their own people. These things have occurred in the course of history. I'm a professional Judge, and I'm a specialist in criminal matters, and I do not exclude any possibility. I have listened to the possibility put forward by the OTP, by the Defence teams, but I could also come up with other possibilities which neither party have put forward. Now as far as these shots are concerned, there has a whole spectrum of possibilities. The fires may have been shot (A), by the HVO; (B), by the HVO; and (C), by the Serbs. You are under oath here. As far as you're concerned, when these shots were fired, when there were civilian casualties as has been tested by some of the documents, where did these shots come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all the time we were waging war with the Serbian side and later with the Muslim side -- that is, not the Muslim side but the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, any fire by the artillery of the HVO was in keeping with the rules that applied to every army, namely targeting positions that issue threats to our own forces. Throughout the fighting between the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was artillery fire from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. Such shelling was especially intense at the time of the conflicts and clashes, at the beginning, that is, and during offensive operations in September by the Army of Republika Srpska against the HVO. The theory that we could have targeted ourselves, I don't know. Perhaps it's theoretically a possibility, but I don't believe it ever happened. I don't believe anyone could have shot at themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand your answer properly, as far as you are concerned, the shots could have only come from the HVO or from the Republika Srpska. You totally exclude the possibility that the Muslims may have caused their own casualties. But you are telling me that when the HVO fired, it fired according to the regulations after having taken all necessary precautions. This is how you answer my question. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning to you. Good morning, Mr. Maric. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now, Mr. Maric, continue with my examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask Honourable Judge Antonetti to turn off his microphone. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will continue the line of questioning following up on Judge Antonetti's questions. These are the most important issues we have to deal with you as a witness. I'll now reorganise my questioning in keeping with that. There were certain inclarities, at least I was unclear. On page 4, line 7, it is recorded that you were talking about offensive operations by the Army of Republika Srpska in September.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September I meant the offensive operations of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll show documents that relate to that, but let us say that it is the Prosecution's claim in the indictment that during a year of conflicts between HVO and the ABH in Eastern Mostar, around 135 civilians were killed. The exact formulation of the Prosecution is at least 135 civilians in a year. Let us try, Mr. Maric, to define the area of Eastern Mostar. As native of that area, could you tell us what is the length of the municipality of Mostar on the eastern side of the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I consider to be the city itself is the length of about 4, 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality would be 20 or so kilometres. Twenty something, maybe 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And as Judge Antonetti said and according to the documents we have in evidence, we could conclude that the most intense shelling from HVO positions took place in September and the first half of October 1993. Can you tell us whether at this time in the whole territory of the municipality of Mostar there were any combat activities between the ABH and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the time of the most intense planned attacks in the area of Mostar by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were any actions actually executed or were they only planned?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The actions that I am referring to were indeed carried out, and at the beginning they scored some successes, but with superhuman efforts the HVO managed to stop these attacks. And in those places where we had lost some positions, we managed to recover them after a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In these actions, did the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina use mortars and other artillery to target HVO positions?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all these operations carried out at that time, activities were carried out in keeping with all the rules of offensive operations. That means including intensive use of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In these offensive operations, did only local forces of the ABH take part or were the Mostar forces reinforced by some outside forces?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these offensive operations of the BH Army, the focal activities were carried out by forces that were introduced from the north towards Mostar, and of course supported by the forces from Mostar itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us precisely which places in the north you mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's my birthplace. I know it very well. That was the axis from Vrdi, the Raska Gora plateau, Rastani, the axes in Mostar itself, and especially a very strategic place in Mostar which is the Hum hill. Those were the axes of fiercest attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, I didn't ask you about the axes of attack. I was trying to find out from where in the north did fresh forces come to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether forces from Sarajevo were expected to come to Mostar as well?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These operations also involved units from other areas. From what I know, Sarajevo and even Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which army do you mean when you say that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 6th Corps from Jablanica, parts of the 1st Corps from Sarajevo, and the 7th Muslim Brigade, which was based, as far as I know, in Zenica, as well as parts of other assault units of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, at the time of these offensive operations, did the BH Army ever experience shortages of ammunition that would force them to stop their attack because they didn't have the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the entirety of these operations and the intensity of the attacks by the BH Army, it is my conclusion that they were never short of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at a couple of documents at the end of your binder, behind the last green divider. 4D741 will be the first document. This is a protest by a liaison officer for the UNPROFOR, dated 31st August 1993, wherein the UNPROFOR is informed that the BH Army targeted and hit the base of the operation zone. Where was the base of the command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, is this report correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you personally remember this incident when a shell hit the command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there at the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 4D1702. This document was written by Sefer Halilovic and approved by Rasim Delic. It's a map showing the plan of the offensive operation called Neretva. Mr. Maric, have you ever heard about this operation of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the course of proofing, did you have occasion to see this map on the computer, including an enlargement of the area around Mostar, indicating exact directions of attack?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us if the offensive operation by the BH Army was actually carried out on these precise axes as shown on the map?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 4D778. This is Sefer Halilovic's document sent to the command of the 1st Corps. This is a request for a unit to urgently be sent to the Neretva Valley. My question to you, sir, is this: Where was the command of the 1st Corps of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 1st Corps was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, what would you say about the engagement of the BiH units from Sarajevo in the attack operations along the Neretva Valley?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the intentions of the BiH Army during that operation were to take the area at all cost and create preconditions for further attacks southward.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the two following documents and then I will have some questions for you. The first one is 4D1719, 1719. This is an order issued by the Chief of the Main Staff, Mr. Zarko Tole, dated the beginning of September 1993. According to General Praljak, Zarko Tole was in charge of the area of Mostar in the Main Staff. I don't have the time to go through everything. However, it is clear from the documents that based on that order the commander of the operation zone, Miljenko Lasic, issued his own order which is P4743. With regard to the two documents, I'm going to ask you this: Were you familiar with Miljenko Lasic's order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. Kim West for the Office of the Prosecution. Just a brief comment, Your Honour. I've noticed this morning there have been at least -- this is the third time that counsel has made statements on the record. The first time she made a statement regarding the number of killed in East Mostar. The second time, she made a statement regarding offensive shelling from the ABiH in late September -- late September and early October. And this is the third time where she's making a statement in regard to the documents. I would just ask counsel to decline from making affirmative statements of fact on the record. Those are not evidence. The only evidence is that which is coming from the witness himself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do take into account what has just been said, Mrs. Alaburic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the objection is not founded. I believe that I have the right to explain for the benefit of the witness all the circumstances that precede a question. What I did was I quote some parts of the indictment, and I believe that this is my right. My right is to precede every question with the relevant portions of the indictment because this will also be relevant when the testimony if -- of this witness is evaluated. I've not suggested an answer to him, I just worded my question a certain way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you say that you had received this order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, my fellow Judge is about to intervene, but let me say this: Ms. West said, quoting several examples, but I'm going to take one. You talk about an offensive operation, page 10, line 7. Therefore, you infer that there was an offensive operation. That may not be what the document says. So then you have to tell witness, "This is an order by Halilovic. Is it or was it an offensive or a defensive action in your view?" And the witness would say, "This was an offensive action." And then you can carry on, take it from there. So this is purely forensic. We're not going to waste any time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I was advising you, Ms. Alaburic, more or less in the same line. It's enough that you mention each time, according to such and such, that is supposed to have happened. Then it's not you who make a statement, but you do what you said you wanted to do. It's -- perhaps with a little linguistic oil it goes down the throat of the Prosecution too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept your suggestion. I believe that I'm very fair. I'm trying very hard not to violate the rules of this court.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you will remember the map issued by Sefer Halilovic and approved by Rasim Delic. If you see arrows on such a map, what do such arrows signify?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such arrows signify the axis of attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When we say "axis of attack," do we qualify this attack as an attack to defend the territory or an attack with an intention to conquer or launch an aggression? What is the meaning of an axis of attack?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, based on this map and the situation on the ground as it was at the time, the axis of attack meant taking control of the area of another side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is exactly how I interpret this term. If we had a representative of the BiH Army, he would say that this was a liberation. A representative of the HVO would say that this was aggression against the territory under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the orders. You said that you had received Miljenko Lasic's order here. In this order first issued by Zarko Tole and then by Miljenko Lasic, it is said that the MOS forces are planning general offensive activities along the whole -- the length of the front line. According to what you know, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just need to have a clarification. I -- I see page 12, line 2, Ms. Alaburic indicating this is exactly how to interpret this term. If we had a representative of the BH Army he would say that it was a liberation. A representative of the HVO would say that this was aggression against the territory under the control of the HVO. It's just unclear to me. I don't understand if this is a question, if this is another affirmative statement, and if we can clarify that so the record is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do that gladly. Gladly. I believe that it was very clear from my addressing the Trial Chamber that the three sentences refer to the instructions that been given to me with regard to the use of certain terms. My questions to the witness were put in order to explain to the Trial Chamber what my intentions were. I did not want to embark on any discussion about the topic of liberation, aggression, or any other qualifications. This was just a continuation of my communication with the Trial Chamber, or, rather, communication between the Trial Chamber and all the parties to the proceedings, including Mrs. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My further questions under item 6 of Mr. Tole's order, it says -- according to you, Mr. Maric, when you read this what are the activities that the HVO is preparing?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO forces, according to this order, under item 6, where it says: "Continue defensive engineering work and antipersonnel obstacle construction ..." This means that they have to continue reinforcing their defence lines and also allow for the possibility to raise obstacles before the defence lines in order to thwart any possible attacks. The intention was to defend themselves, exclusively that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D786 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] There doesn't seem to be any interpretation. Sorry. This was an ancillary question of interest to me in Mr. Tole's document, under number 1. Witness, look at Mr. Tole's document. Under number 1, the troops or units are ordered to be brought up to full combat readiness immediately. So upon reading this, I wonder whether at the time the situation was not such that everybody was positioned on the ground depending on or according to the military space, and that there were, every now and then, tensions and that everybody then was requested to get into full combat readiness, which may mean for any judge who would think about the situation, that the situation, the military situation, was quiet most of the time and that there were, every now and then, incidents that would cause everybody to be put on alert or mobilised, or was it then a situation of full combat in which it was a situation of permanent mobilisation. I may be wrong, but the first point here seems to say that there is a mobilisation but following an event which was no doubt the Neretva operation. Could you shed some light on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the HVO use some of its units to hold the lines facing the BiH Army and the Army of Republika Srpska. Based on the intelligence received, they expected somewhat stronger attacks in this particular area. And the way I interpret item 1 is that the Main Staff, based on that intelligence calls for full combat readiness because they estimated that the attacks would be so strong that it would be -- that this would be the only way to defend the front line. I would like to mention that the focal points of the -- the attacks, if there were any successes, would mean that the defence lines of the HVO facing the BiH Army would crumble very soon. Especially the Vrdi access was very sensitive because of the configuration of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, is there a difference between an order to raise combat readiness and an order to launch a certain combat operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An order to raise combat readiness means that all the elements of a unit should be raised to such a level of preparedness that they can be used should that become necessary, and an order to launch an attack implies the drafting of certain combat documents which expressly assign tasks -- tasks to certain elements in every unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document: 4D786. This a BiH Army document issued on 11 September 1993, where it says an order to attack in an operation under the name "The Defence of people's rights, Vrdi 1993." Mr. Maric, did you ever hear of such an operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of this order you can see the axis of attack. From your recollection, can you tell us whether this reflects the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that the attack followed. All that is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document: 4D1722. This is another order by the chief of Main Staff, Zarko Tole, and after that let's look at 4D1547. This is an identical order which was issued by the commander of the operation zone and sent to his units. Mr. Maric, were you familiar with this order issued by your commander of the operation zone?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the introduction it says that the Muslim forces have prepared all-out offensive activities in all front lines, including Dreznica, Vrdi, Mostar, Buna, and Dubrava. The locations that I have just mentioned, were they in the territory of your operation zone?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in the territory of the operation zone South-east Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In mid-September 1993, was the BiH Army undertaking attacks in that area?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were the -- those attacks undertaken in order to take over the control of the territory that were under the HVO control, or alternatively, was that the defence of BH Army-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was about their desire to take over the control of the territories that had been under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 6 of Zarko Tole's order it says: "Urgently invest efforts to reinforce defence points in depth." Could you please describe the HVO activities in some more detail?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, just like in the previous orders where warnings were issued and troops alerted to carry out engineering efforts to reinforce the defence line, and as regards the reinforcement in depth, for us soldiers the worst task was to carry out engineering works in depth, because that meant and that informed us that there was danger of losing territories as a result of fierce attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Witness, I am trying to interpret this document politically. If the information received by Mr. Tole is correct, because obviously he has received intelligence from the intelligence services saying that there was an offensive, but under points 2 and 3 explaining the order, there seems to be a co-ordination between the VRS and -- and the ABiH. Based on this, I suppose that the military part, that is, Halilovic and on the other side we have Mladic, that they must have tried to cover their backs, politically speaking, by including Izetbegovic and Karadzic into the operation. In your view, when Mr. Tole said that there was co-ordination between the RS, Republika Srpska, and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, does this have a political dimension?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What dimension is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because you answered yes, so I asked you what kind of political dimension or meaning do you see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, we know reliably that meetings were held between local political leaders from Mostar and the leaders of the Army of Republika Srpska, as well as certain political circles from the neighbouring municipalities such as Nevesinje. The topic at these meetings was co-operation, primarily military co-operation, in order to inflict the worst possible damage to HVO forces. I didn't go into any deeper analysis of their political co-operation, not then and not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are therefore telling me that you know that the regional political leaders met to address the issue. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document, 4D1219. This is a schematic showing offensive operations by the BH Army in Eastern Mostar and Mostar in the middle of the month of September 1993. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. We want to avoid further problems should you seek to admit the document. I don't know whether you want to seek its admission or not. Can you tell us who established -- who drafted the document, ABiH, VRS, HVO?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is one of a series of such maps which we wanted to use to show you, in a very simple way, the events on the ground. Several of these have already admitted -- have been already admitted into evidence, including this one, my colleague just advised me. It is already an exhibit. All these maps have been prepared by the Defence team of General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, but can you tell me whether it was General Petkovic in person who put the various colours on it, you know, and the arrows as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most often we worked in this way: General Petkovic would draw up all the essential things, the locations of various forces and the directions they were moving, and then the actual placing of these positions on a -- in a wider area was done at a lower level, to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Maric, to the best of your knowledge, does this map accurately reflect the events on the ground in the middle of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very simple way of showing it, but to me, who knows exactly what it was, it's quite clear that all the axes of attacks by the BH Army on the HVO are very well shown very accurately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And the last document we prepared for your testimony, 4D793. This is a document from Arif Pasalic, 20th September 1993. I will read out two statements to you and ask you for a comment. The commander of the 4th Corps of the BH Army says, this is the middle of the first passage: "Solid territory of the BH Army, that is the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is growing by the hour." Was the BH Army indeed spreading the territory under its control in Mostar at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time when this document was written, the BH Army has taken hold of certain territories that we were holding until then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: He then says that the positions of the BH Army were moving forward in the south, north, and centre, including the capturing of some very important elevations of strategic importance, and he says that there is street-to-street fighting in Mostar and combat is continuing full steam. Is this statement by the BH Army commander correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is all I have planned, Your Honours, for my examination on the subject. We have a vast quantity of documents that we haven't shown, but I think this will suffice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, but I'll first give the floor to my fellow Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, I see this report where the commander of a corps of the army -- Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, reports that the territory under control of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is growing. Now, where are we politically and legally? Where is all this taking place? On the territory of which entity, which state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All this is happening in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Is it then not absolutely legitimate that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina recovers the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, not for a moment did I have a feeling that I did not belong to the units that were defending the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Therefore, I cannot accept that I was not defending the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina regardless of the fact that I was defending it from within the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I want to make it clear, sir. You are here as a witness. You are not accused. This is not about your -- the wrongfulness of your personal activities, so do not, please, feel attack and do not think that you have to defend your own dealings. I find it a bit confusing to see that apparently the units of the Federal Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, an internationally recognised state with a government, are defending the territory of that entity, and the HVO also claims to be defending the territorial integrity of that entity. Somehow this seems to me rather absurd. I wonder whether you can de-absurdise or rationalise, explain this situation in a way, or tell me why I am -- I am in error in finding this somewhat absurd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been repeating from the start, everyone whoever commanded me and every assignment I ever got pursued one purpose, to defend the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I never held any political position, nor could I ever evaluate this from a political point of view. When we were attacked, it was my assignment and the assignment of my units to defend ourselves. I never bothered myself with political connotations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I would appreciate it if you could give me leave to ask just a few follow-up questions on the questions of Judge Trechsel, and then you can go on asking questions of another nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have no time for political subjects, and I don't think I should discuss them with soldiers, but I will nevertheless, Mr. Maric - and I apologise for this - ask you this: Did you personally hold that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was protecting the interests of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not infer that from their activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you believe that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was protecting the interests of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which interests of which ethnic community did you believe the BH Army to have defended?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Bosniak people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if somebody suggested that the BH Army alone in Bosnia and Herzegovina defended the interests of all the peoples, all the ethnic communities of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the entire state, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree any time, because every time I get up and -- or sit down, I still feel all the consequences of my fighting to -- to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina. It had an impact on my health and took a toll.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how were you wounded? From a -- by a bullet from which army?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded in the middle of November 1993, by an enemy shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From which positions or which direction did the shell come from?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I do not care, and I would rather that it had come from Serbian positions, but from all I know, I have reason to believe it had come from the positions of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, thank you for allowing me these few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, as far as the document is concerned, I was looking at the B/C/S version and the English translation of this document. General Pasalic, who has died, while we've already seen videos of this gentleman, we've seen him in contact with General Petkovic and the HVO. Seemingly, we had the feeling that the relationship between Mr. Pasalic and the officers of the HVO was good, all the more since they had fought together. In this document, he signs the following, we are the 20th of September. It is 1900 hours, and he says as follows: That the extremists of the HVO and of the Croatian Army have not abided by the cease-fire that they had signed, and in the morning, they shelled the defence lines in Mostar in the area of -- area of responsibility of the 4th Corps. Together with the artillery, hundreds of shells are coming from the tanks, howitzers, and mortars. What I'm struck with in this text is why he qualifies the extremists of the HVO and of the Croatian Army. It seems that -- but unfortunately he will never be able to tell us what he actually meant since he is no longer alive. But when I read this text, I feel that in his mind he felt that there was the HVO and the Croatian Army and extremists and that these are the troublemakers. What do you think of this? Is the document not lying, because you have shelled and attacked, and why does he mark this distinction between extremists and those people who were not extremists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm of the opinion that with this rhetoric, Mr. Pasalic was just trying to give a different tone to this report. As for this theory that there was a regular army as opposed to some extremists, I cannot believe it. That is how I see this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, as far as the attack conducted by the HVO is concerned, do you agree with him that on the 20th of September the HVO shelled, thus violating the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree that the HVO opened fire and violated the cease-fire. It simply wasn't possible. They wouldn't have done it if they hadn't come under a threat. I can't remember the day. I don't remember whether there were any combat activities. In any case, the HVO or anybody else could not open fire without any order, and I don't remember any such order, an order to open fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's go back a little and continue where we left it off yesterday, Mr. Maric, mid-March 1993. I'm not going to show you any documents because I want to reduce the number of documents to a minimum. I would like to remind you of Sovici, and you said that Konjic and Jablanica were in your operation zone. You remember you said that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My follow-up question is this: In mid-April of that year, was there any redeployment of the artillery of the operation zone in the areas of Risovac, Sovicka Vrata, and some other localities in the municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A rocket artillery group, or, rather, an artillery firing group was taken out from the artillery of the operation zone and moved to the locality known as Risovac, which was also part of the South-east Herzegovina operations group, and it was there that they took up their firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that redeployment of artillery equipment?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the redeployment of the artillery equipment under the command of the commander was to open fire on military targets along the line from Jablanica to Konjic. The purpose was to relieve the burden and a distraction, as far as possible, and the relief of all the aggressive attacks against the HVO in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, did the HVO have an intention to take the town of Jablanica, to conquer it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not either HVO's intention or something they were able to do. The establishment of a firing group did not mean that there were any guarantees to the HVO that the HVO was in a position to conquer anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were you in Sovici or around Sovici at the time when the HVO carried out the attacks on that village?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was involved in the preparation and transport of that firing group in the direction of Risovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to a different topic. The topic is the 9th of May, 1993, Mostar. Just by way of introduction, let me say something before I show you a couple of documents. Were you in Mostar during the night between the 8th and 9th May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in my own house which was relatively close to the centre of Mostar and the command of the operation zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did something unusual happen that night?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early morning hours I was woken up by the intense fire opened from infantry weapons and sporadic and more frequent detonations of infantry weapons and artillery weapons of low calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What did you do when you heard all that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I had means to communicate with the command of the of the military district. I called the duty officer. I -- Mr. Bozo Raguz replied. I was the first one to call him. I asked him what was going on. With some trepidation and nervousness in his voice he said, "I don't know what's going on. It seems that we are under attack." I immediately got up, got dressed, and from the moment I woke up to the moment I arrived at the command of the military district was about 20 minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How many people were already there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The customary number of officers were there at the communications centre and the logistics centre. Some five or six officers were there, as was the custom at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What does it mean when you say "the customary number"? Customary for what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the number that would have been present there in peacetime. Officers on duty, a minimum number of officers on duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Maric, can you tell us at what time you arrived at the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime after 5.00 in the morning. 5.15, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The commander of the operation zone, was he there at the command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As soon as I arrived at the command, I asked the duty officer, Raguz, whether he had spoken to the commander of the military district. His answer was, "Yes, I spoke to him at his home in Siroki Brijeg, and he told me that he would be there immediately."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did Lasic indeed come?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lasic came some 40 minutes or so after me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us briefly, what did the commander of the operation zone do when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he arrived, his first reaction was to ask us whether we had established communication with all the units on the ground, whether we had managed to obtain information as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to the initial information from the ground, what was going on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that we knew with some certainty was the fact that in the direction of Liska, Ulica, Zahum, and Podhum, groups from the direction of the hitherto BiH camps where units of BH Army had been deployed until then, that infantry groups started marching from those camp areas. Then Commander Lasic went to the communications centre, and for some 15 minutes or so we were separated. I was in my own office reflecting upon the situation at hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The infantry groups of the BH Army, did they enjoy any artillery support?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were supported mostly by 60- and 82-millimetre mortar fire and other tools that an infantry group can have on its strength such as Zoljas, RPGs, and similar tools.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the first order issued to HVO units at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first verbal order that I heard from Commander Lasic was to engage on the axis of attack and to establish communication with all the subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you know and if you remember, what was the goal of the HVO engagement at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal of the HVO unit and group engagement at the time, those who could react most rapidly in Mostar, was to stop further advancement in depth of the territory in the western part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether there was a plan to push back the BiH Army units.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were trying to devise a plan to stop the attacks, we were also trying to devise a plan to push back the infiltrated groups and other BH Army units on the axis of attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the position to which BiH Army groups and units had to be pushed back to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since at the time there was no separation line between the BH Army and the HVO in any classical military terms, there were no military positions that could be construed as part of the military activities involving the HVO and BiH Army. The focus was Bulevar road. That was the area which lended itself to establishing a temporary defence line.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is that the separation line that had been agreed already in April between the BiH Army and the HVO under the auspices of UNPROFOR? You mentioned Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At that moment did the HVO also take a decision to take any BiH Army facilities or positions?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since we managed to stop the attack and since we managed to almost completely push the BiH Army units back to their starting positions, it was decided to take the Vranica building and the command of the 4th Corps of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, was any HVO attack targeted at any other facilities but military facilities?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment the focus was put on pushing the units back and returning the positions. There was no intention or order to attack any other military or other facilities save for the command of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, did there come a time on the 9th of May for you to see an unusually large group of people gathering in the vicinity of the Velez football pitch?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the command on two occasions only briefly, and I did have an opportunity to see groups of people moving more or less in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know why those people were there, in the vicinity of the Velez football pitch?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of all the reasons. However, in passing, I did ask a few acquaintances where they were going and what was going on, and the answer was, "Let me be. You go down there and stay alive." Those were mostly residents of those neighbourhoods where combat had started that same morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did any of the members of the civilian or military structures of the HVO ever tell you what the whole thing was all about, why those people were there in the first place?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I knew at the time, it was all a matter of prevention. Civilians were being evacuated from the area of war activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the bus depot in Mostar, where is it located?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus depot is 70 metres away from the football pitch, and the parking lot is adjacent to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you say that buses were parked there every night and, if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the case even before the war. All the buses belonging to the city transport authorities were parked in that locality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, under the assumption that people had arrived in the Velez football pitch in order to be evacuated from Mostar and that this should have been done through the engagement of a large number of buses, would it have taken a long time for the buses to be provided and put into that use?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't have taken long at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long would it have taken? Would it have sufficed for the bus drivers to be called and for the engines to be turned on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would very much sum it up. The drivers would have to be called and that's all. The drivers in that company had already been mobilised and they had already been duty-bound to use the buses as necessary and as they were told.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if the HVO ever managed to take the Vranica building which housed the command of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The HVO took the Vranica building in the course of the following day, if I remember properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the course of the following day, did the intensity of fighting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mrs. Alaburic. We're going to stop now because it's 10.30. The questions are important, of course. I shall not fail to put some of the questions myself, but as far as the time left, I believe you have something like 20 minutes left, perhaps even less than that. Our Registrar, who is back, will tell you exactly how much time you have left, which means that you will be able over the break to put in the right order those documents you wish to show to the witness in those 20 minutes you have left. And I will also have questions to put to the witness, because this is an extremely important topic. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Please, Ms. Alaburic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since I have only 18 minutes left and some other events and some other dates, in our view, are more important for the Petkovic Defence than the 9th of May, 1993, I don't have more questions about that topic, and since you told us that you might have some questions about that date, I would like to give you the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I listened to the questions and the answers very carefully. The date of the 9th of May is a very relevant date for the OTP. In the indictment, the Prosecution says that there were events that took place in Mostar on the 9th of May and that involved consequences as part of a joint criminal enterprise. Let us take the case in which the HVO allegedly attacked the ABiH. In that case, would there have been a phase of preparation with orders involved, among other things, concerning the positions to be taken by the artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are under oath, and I ask whether prior to the 9th of May there existed this type of orders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there are two options, Colonel. Either you are telling the truth and the Prosecution case has to collapse inevitably, because then it was not the HVO but the ABiH that launched the attack, or you're not telling the truth. So I'm going to try and dig deeper. If -- as I understood you told us that between 4.00 and 5.00 in the morning you were asleep, you were in bed, when you heard shooting. Then you rang Raguz, who was the duty officer, and straightaway you went to the operational centre, the operations room, where Mr. Lasic was not present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had the HVO attacked - this is an if, of course - would Mr. Lasic have been present at the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as I understand, he was, like you were, in bed, he was in bed when you were woken up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was woken up by detonations, and Mr. Lasic, our commander, got a telephone call because his house was about 30 kilometres away from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So he was 30 kilometres from Mostar. You are a military man. You are highly trained, and we have to look at it from a purely military point of view. In military terms, can it be imagined that the HVO commander would be absent, that the defence minister would be absent, that the commander of the operation zone would be absent, that the one in charge of artillery would be absent? In military terms, is it conceivable that all these individuals would be absent and that there would be an HVO offensive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be inconceivable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the HVO had attacked, I suppose that there would have been preparatory meetings, because the Main Staff of the ABiH that was in West Mostar would have been taken control of. There would be a host of -- of orders, I suppose. I suppose that there would be an increased degree of mobilisation of the soldiers, and I suppose also that everybody would have been there with their full kit all prepared on the ground. In military terms, should that have been the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let leave this part aside. Regarding the Velez stadium and the buses you said something important, and I must say I hadn't seen that before, whilst it is important. You gave a minor detail. Maybe it was not really seen in its full importance, but for me it is important. Based on the indictment and the pre-trial brief of the Prosecutor, I thought that everything had been organised, and, among other things, that the buses had been requisitioned, and I thought, so far, that these were private buses belonging to a private company. In other words, that would have involved quite a degree of organisation. And you said before, and this is the first time I hear this, and we've been in trial for over four years, you said two important things. Firstly, that the buses were all parked next to the stadium. That was always so. And secondly, you added that, as a matter of fact, these were buses that belonged to the public transport company. In other words, they were there. And the bus drivers, who were staff members of that company, they were available. As far as you know, is this the way it took place, the buses were there and they could, if need be, transport people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The buses were there, as I've told you, even before the war for a number of years. The main bus depot in Mostar is some 70 metres away from the stadium, whereas the big open -- opened area adjacent to the stadium served as the main parking lot for those buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also said another thing that was important. You learned that the people that had been in the stadium and then put somewhere else, that was part of the civilian evacuation because of the fighting. But how can you account for the fact that a number of these people ended at the Heliodrom and that some stayed there for some length of time? You may not have an answer to this, but how is it that people one sought to protect and evacuate from places where there was fighting ended up "detained" or imprisoned? I'm not using any of these specific terms, but that a certain number of these people ended up at the Heliodrom? And in some very few cases, they were very elderly people, even a few children. Not many of them, but a few. So how do you account for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my explanation is as follows: Heliodrom is a large plateau with facilities which were virtually empty. Only a few were being used. The area was secure, which means that there were conditions in place for the safe evacuation of a certain number of civilians to save them from the threat of combat or any other negative external influences in the area. That is my opinion and my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We know about the Heliodrom because the Judges went there and visit the facilities. Indeed, it's rather large.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, you have said that you talked to certain people that were marching towards the Velez stadium. Do you have an impression, an idea or a knowledge of how these people were ethnically composed? Were they half Muslim, half Croat? Were they mainly Croat? Were they mainly Serbs perhaps? Do you have any idea about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the people I met and the ten of them or so that I recognised, there were six to seven Muslims and around three Croats I know personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of those Croats that you know personally and that were led to the Velez stadium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Pehar, Zorica something. Her last name I don't know. And they lived close to the Bulevar in Liska Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is important because this is the very first time we've heard about this. You gave names and you said that among the ten people that you came across who were on their way to the stadium there were Croats. So they were made to leave the place. Were they put into the Heliodrom or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I had no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned ten or so people you came across. Were they being taken towards the Heliodrom under the threat of a gun or a rifle, or was it by word of mouth, that it had been said that they had to leave and go towards the Velez stadium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I sent [as interpreted] them when they were on the move, going in the direction of the Velez stadium. I cannot give you any details because I don't know any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you have 18 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one correction. Page 37, line 7. It's recorded that the witness said "I sent them," and the witness actually said "I saw them," to avoid any confusion about the role of Mr. Maric.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Maric, let us go very briefly through some important events in Mostar after these clashes on the 9th and 10th of May. I have prepared a set of documents about May. Now, rely on the monitor, because I can't give you any instructions, any references for the binder. This will concern the situation in Mostar after the 9th of May. The first document is 4D1680. It's a report by the commander of the operation zone, dated 14 May, concerning the situation in Mostar, and the report says that in the city of Mostar occasional shooting can be heard, and in conclusion it says it's relatively quiet. The next document is 4D1681.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. Would you please give us some time to find these documents. There are somewhere here, but it's not easy to locate because they're not in an order. They're in the order you planned to present them, but now we have to -- to check to find these documents. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we may go on, the next document is 1681, a report from Miljenko Lasic for the 15th of May. It is noted that things are relatively quiet. And going on in all reports for May the same statement is made. Mr. Maric, are these indeed reports by the commander of your operation zone?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are the estimates correct as stated in the reports, that the situation was relatively quiet?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you had to describe briefly that May in Mostar, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground the situation was getting calmer and calmer every day, and people were beginning to feel a dose of optimism, that perhaps there is peace in the foreseeable future.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, approximately how long did this relative peace continue in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May and June approximately, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Maric, on document 1681, Mr. Lasic reports a heavy mortar attack on the Tihomir Misic Barracks. Is that consonant with the idea that the situation was calm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to some extent it is not consonant, but the Tihomir Misic Barracks is a bit away from the city, so the situation in the populated area was quiet, and to us it was of great importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would also like to ask a question from you about the same document. Then in, I believe, one, two, three, four, five -- then the fourth line of that very document, then it is said: "UNPROFOR came to Konjic yesterday but failed to enter Croatian villages in this area." My question is: If -- what was the cause, why UNPROFOR failed to enter Croatian villages? Is it because they were not allowed to do so and to go there, or for whatever -- any other reason which then prevented them to enter Croatian villages? I wonder if it is clear to you what my question is aimed at. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those Croatian villages were completely encircled by the BH Army. I don't know why the army didn't allow them into those Croatian villages. It's certain that HVO could not prevent them from going in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Honourable Judge Trechsel drew your attention to this part of Lasic's report about the attacks by the BH Army on the Tihomir Misic Barracks. If we also look at the other reports by Lasic, we would see that on other days there were similar attacks on the barracks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period from the 9th May until the 30th of May, 17 members of the HVO were killed by BH Army snipers, including 11 who were my close friends or acquaintances. Those were mainly sniper attacks from positions in Zalik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, if a military report refers to relative peace, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that there is no combat activity that could result in movements of front line, but there may be sporadic fire to harass the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct on the premise that the BH Army is attacking the barracks while it is quiet in other parts of Mostar, would it be correct to call that situation relative peace?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was called relative peace, and there was an amount of wishful thinking in that. Everyone wanted that to turn into real peace. However, later developments demonstrated that those sniper attacks on the barracks pursued the aim of demoralising the troops in the barracks, because it's quite a lot for 17 young men to be killed within a month.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Maric, after the clashes on the 9th of May in Mostar, is it the case that a large number of Muslim members started leaving the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the conflict on the 9th of May, some members of the HVO of Muslim ethnicity began to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, how did the HVO treat its own members who wanted to leave?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very fairly, in keeping with all the rules on demobilisation, but there was a lot of emotion on the part of lower-level commanders who had spent a lot of time shoulder to shoulder with those men fighting a common enemy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You referred to the rules on demobilisation. Does that mean that those young men who wanted to leave were simply demobed? Is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At their own request they returned to supply all their equipment and weapons, and were issued appropriate certificates, after which they were free to go wherever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness. In the translation this is not quite clear. They returned to supply their equipment. Does that mean that they rendered, they gave back their equipment, or does it mean that they -- they sort of were allowed to keep their equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those who wanted to be relieved of duty, and that was only a part of them, had to return to supplies their equipment and weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's now correct, return to supplies, to a special place. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We still have to look at a number of documents. 4D1180 will be the first. Mr. Maric, you look at the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for Your Honours, it's in the same set, several documents behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This is an approval of a commander, a brigade commander, for the demobilisation of a soldier -- of some soldiers of Muslim ethnicity judging by names, and this specifies that the soldiers had returned the weapons and equipment they had been issued with at their unit. Mr. Maric, was this indeed the proper procedure, when a soldier wanted to leave at his own request, he would hand back his weapon and be demobed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was the unit commander indeed authorised to approve, authorise or not authorise?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the unit commander had that right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D1225 is the next document. Also from the 2nd Brigade of the HVO, the unit commander proposes demobilisation for a number of soldiers of Muslim ethnicity due to their failure to report to the unit. It's dated 14 June 1993. Tell us, Mr. Maric, was it indeed the procedure for demobilising soldiers who were simply not showing up anymore?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure. The list would, of course, be sent to the department that monitored the strength of the unit so that all the benefits and pay and payroll would be adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What happened with the equipment and weapons of these soldiers who simply stopped showing up?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be properly stored in the appropriate facilities of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I don't think you understood my question. Let's assume we have a soldier who simply stopped coming back to the unit. What happened with the equipment and weapon of that soldier?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the equipment that was on the person of that soldier at the moment when he stopped coming back to the unit remained in his possession. My first answer referred to the other procedure, the proper procedure when authorisation was given and weapons were returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the HVO to Muslim soldiers who remained in HVO units?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were treated like any other member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did anyone in the HVO make any sort of trouble to a Muslim soldier who want to stay on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any such case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And now tell me, Mr. Maric, for you in Mostar, the date of 30th June 1993, is it memorable in any way?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. That was an important date, a hugely important date for Mostar. That night all the chances for the peace we had so wished for were buried. I don't know which minds planned on that night that some Muslims within the HVO in cahoots with members of the BH Army, mainly locals from Bijelo Polje who that night were at their homes, should attack the command and the troops of the HVO, mainly the 2nd Brigade, also the area of Rastani and the Tihomir Misic Barracks. That night, to our astonishment - and we have to blame also our bad evaluations - some HVO members of Muslim ethnicity turned against us, changed their insignia, and attacked the men they had served together with until the day before.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, I'll tell you now how General Praljak characterised that date, that day, and I will ask for your comment. He said that was the beginning of all-out war in Mostar between HVO and the BH Army. Would that qualification be accurate, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is very accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, thanks to these events on the 30th June, capture the territory to the north of Mostar, towards Jablanica and east of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night, the BH Army took control of the territory from the beginning, that is, the North Camp, Carina, Zalik, Rastani, Vrapcici, all of Bijelo Polje, and further to the north towards Dreznica and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, Mr. Maric, after that 30th of June, if anyone wanted to go from Eastern Mostar to Jablanica, was he able to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was able.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any civilian or a serviceman who -- who was killed on the Mostar-Jablanica road as a result of artillery fire or any other fire opened by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such instance. I'm not aware of any such case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at another document speaking about communication between Mostar and Jablanica that I deem to be the most relevant. I am going to skip everything else that I wanted to present about that topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is in the set of documents, third from the last.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maric, you can listen to me. The document number is 4D719. It is already in evidence, and I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, your time is up. Please try to conclude now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, Your Honour. I will just have one more question about this communication and that will bring me to an end.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document, and you can listen to me, Mr. Maric, the chief of the staff for the 4th Corps of the BH Army in mid-October 1993 says, amongst other things, that it is necessary to stop traffic along the road during the changeover of men from this company, and the sentence goes on but I will finish it here. In your view, Mr. Maric, what does this sentence mean when it says in terms of traffic along the way? Is there any traffic or not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was traffic along that highway, and this points to the fact that it was so heavy that at certain moments it could even hinder the regular changeovers of the BiH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Further on this report says, and I quote: "The transport of civilian population and others who are marching in the direction of north and south is a big problem for us. That's why the organs of civilian authorities should take over the transport of civilians." According to what you know, Mr. Maric, if a civilian from East Mostar wanted to go to Jablanica, for example, did they have an ability to do that? Could they do that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Further on it says there are major problems in the transport of the wounded and others, and an APC has to be repaired for night use. Did you know that the BH Army transported its wounded to the hospital in town?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says further on that there is a major problem with the supply of the BiH units with bread, because wood for the bakery has to be transported to Mostar and then bread has to be transported to Bijelo Polje. In your view, does this confirm or deny the possibility that there was communication between Mostar and Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: VINKO MARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This confirms the possibility of communication between Mostar and Bijelo Polje and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
